text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The rising value of the ringgit against the U.S. dollar is no cause for worry, said Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
-- A concerted effort will be made to reduce traffic woes throughout Malaysia, said Anwar.
-- Contributors to the state pension fund, the Employees Provident Fund, will receive a monthly pension instead of lump sum payments, under a proposed scheme by the government.
-- Local and international companies can start applying to participate in Malaysia's telecommunications and information technology backbone, the Multimedia Super Corridor, from next month.
-- The alleged kidnap of a Malaysian forestry worker in Zimbabwe by Angolan separatists has not been verified by the Malaysian High Commission in Harare.
-- Privatised sewerage concession holder Indah Water Konsortium Sdn Bhd is to invest around 1.8 billion ringgit between now and the year 2001, said its chairman Wan Adli Wan Ibrahim.

-- Two Americans facing charges of attempting to defraud Malaysian government-owned Bank Bumiputra Malaysia Bhd of $600 million have have been ordered to appear in a Pennsylvania state court on April 7, said Assistant U.S. Attorney William Behe.
